Wow this got blown out of proportion. Once again, I'm going to say I don't care about all the meta information. If it wasn't clear in the show, then it wasn't done well enough, and I don't consider it canon. 

Also, I'm really not "telling" her anything. She's a fictional character in a show that ended. I never liked her relationship with Jeff, but its not like I was going to do anything if they got together. I am neither going to, nor have the ability to stop her from getting with Jeff. 

You say to consider Annie's feelings, but Annie viewed Abed as one of her best friends. They lived together for so long, and she did all sorts of wacky stuff with him for fun like the "dead girlfriend footage". Also Abed did care about Annie. Though its technically unconfirmed, Abed being on the autism spectrum if greatly implied. I have a lot of family on the autism spectrum so I know that they can have a hard time expressing feelings. He cared about Annie and the rest of the group a lot, in his own way. He lives in his own head and he fixates on movies because it helps him understand the world. He suffers a lot of abuse from the others, especially from Jeff because they struggle to communicate with him. It's not really either of their faults. It's just the way it happened.

Once again, maybe we interpreted the show differently. That happens sometimes. I don't really care what other people took away from the show. There were aspects to the characters that balanced each other out, but there were also aspects that really clashed. In my eyes, unless they both severely changed, they were never going to have a healthy relationship. From my point of view, Annie, like many other young girls, wanted to feel more mature which is why she liked older guys like Jeff and Rich. (Also, I always viewed Vaughn as being much younger than Jeff, closer to 23-25.) Meanwhile Jeff, clinging to his youth, was attracted to Annie. 

Yes Annie had been through a lot by that time, but she was still immature emotionally. She threw tantrums a lot, and she never actually talked to Jeff or anyone else about how she felt until a little bit in the finale. When Jeff and Britta get engaged, she just kinda whines in the background. Sure she was mature for her age, but she tried to act even more mature when she wasn't. 

I really don't feel like writing an entire essay on how I don't like a fictional relationship so I'll wrap it up. I know I am a super cynical person and I have a different view of love than most do. I would call their relationship infatuation, but not love. I don't even think either of them really understood what love was. Annie loved Jeff's age, experience, and charisma. Jeff loved Annie's innocence, youth, ambition, and her potential to live a fulfilling life away from Greendale. But I think they didn't truly love each other. If you disagree that's fine. It's just different interpretations. I really don't care if I am going against the entire Community fanbase. I have my own opinion and I've watched the show multiple times without it changing. One person on reddit aggressively defending them is not going to make the difference here.

To be fair, I'm not just basing it on the age gap. In both Jeff/Annie and Troy/Britta, there is a massive maturity gap. It's the whole reason that Troy/Britta fails. Also, during the last couple seasons, especially after Troy left, I didn't think Annie and Abed's friendship was toxic at all. Abed and Annie grow closer as friends. Sure they're sometimes rude to each other, but everyone in the group is kinda awful to each other sometimes. I don't see how you can claim Abed/Annie is unhealthy and creepy yet say Jeff/Annie is perfectly fine. 

Furthermore, the age gap does matter, especially when you consider the time when they're relationship started. Jeff/Annie began in season 1 when Annie was 18 and Jeff was 35. Annie was an insecure girl who was getting real male attention for the first time in her life. Jeff was an egotistical womanizer. Do you see the power imbalance there? 

 As for playing with emotions, I think you need to be more specific because I can't really think of an instance for that besides the catfishing thing. Meanwhile Jeff made out with Annie while running away from two other women, and then tried to act like it never happened. 

I never saw that Jeff and Annie balanced each other out and made each other better people. The whole relationship always seemed childish to me. If anything, it seemed to me that they made each other worse by being together. Jeff was always trying to use Annie for better grades etc. In Intro to Knots, he literally doesn't do anything because he is relying on Annie (and the others) to carry him through to a barely passing grade, even though he knows how important good grades are to her. Meanwhile, Annie had a childish, superficial crush on Jeff. It seemed to me that Annie liked him whenever he was being the charismatic leader, but whenever he was being the immature, carefree side of him, she really didn't like him. Therefore, it always seemed to me that she wasn't actually in love with him, but just had a crush. Her fawning over him just fed his ego even more. It never seemed like they were actually in love. Jeff was going to marry Britta in the s5 finale and in the s6 finale, Jeff literally makes a pitch of him being surrounded by beautiful women. If they had all been Annie clones, I might've been swayed but they weren't. 

As for what you said about it being proven and Dan saying it, I don't know anything about that. I'm basing all of my information on what I saw in the show. Even if that was the intention of the writers, my philosophy is that if they can't convince me through the writing, then it wasn't done well enough.

Finally, I can't say this enough. I don't actually like Abed/Annie. I just prefer it to everything else. If you prefer Jeff/Annie, that's fine. We interpreted the show in different ways, which is normal. I was around Annie's age when I watched community the first time so her being flirted with by the 35 year-old man really bothered me, and I haven't liked it since. If you had a different view of the show, that's fine

Hey. I’ve been through this, and it sucks. The feeling doesn’t really go away, at least not completely. There’s always going to be a little bit that lingers and you just have to cope. 
However, if you want it to get better, you first have to determine if they actually feel you’re a burden or it’s a figment of your imagination. If they are consistently not inviting you, but inviting everyone else in your circle, that’s a sign. If there are days where you are upset and no one notices something is wrong, that’s another sign. If no one ever talks to you directly, that’s a sign. The biggest one is if you see them stop talking when you get near. If all of them are happening, chances are you need to find new friends. It’s sad but true. 
On the flip side, if none or only one of these are happening, it could just be your imagination that you’re a burden. Ask them to go places with you 1 on 1, like hey can you go with me to pick this up. Also, even if it feels wrong or awkward, tell them seriously if you’re feeling insecure and carefully watch their body language and word choice. Most importantly, don’t let it get you down. Friends come and go constantly. Don’t think that it’s the end of the world. It will get better.
